# NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Country** | United States |
| **City** | Pasadena, CA |
| **Tier** | Extended (Tier II) |
| **Primary ecosystem** | Earth / planetary remote sensing |
| **Relevant units** | **JEDI** (Joint Emissivity Database Initiative) · **LST&E Portal** (Land Surface Temperature & Emissivity) |
| **Scale** | Earth-system, multi-mission, multi-decadal |

## Why it matters internationally

JPL is one of the world's leading institutions in the **remote-sensing
branch** of emissivity research. **JEDI** aims to create a unified
land-surface emissivity Earth System Data Record — a long-term, consistent,
calibrated emissivity dataset across multiple sensors and missions — while
the **LST&E Portal** focuses on reconciliation, validation, metadata, and
community use. In materials laboratories emissivity is often measured on
individual samples; at JPL, emissivity is an **Earth-system variable** that
must be retrieved, reconciled, and distributed at scale. Any serious map
of emissivity research that excludes JPL would be incomplete, because it
would omit the entire planetary and Earth-observation branch of the field.

## Scope of activity

### Relevant units

- **JEDI — Joint Emissivity Database Initiative** — unified land-surface
  emissivity Earth System Data Record.
- **LST&E Portal — Land Surface Temperature & Emissivity Portal** —
  reconciliation, validation, metadata, and community use of LST&E
  products.

### Radiative properties measured / retrieved

Land-surface emissivity · land-surface temperature — as retrieved from
satellite thermal-infrared data.

### Capability envelope

- **Wavelength:** thermal infrared.
- **Methodology:** Earth-system emissivity retrieval, reconciliation, and
  long-term data records across multiple missions — **MODIS, AIRS, ASTER,
  VIIRS** — with cross-mission harmonization of LST&E products.

### Signature infrastructure

- **JEDI land-surface emissivity Earth System Data Record** — a unified
  emissivity ESDR drawing on multiple sensors.
- **LST&E Portal** — reconciliation, validation, metadata, and community
  use of land-surface temperature and emissivity products.

### Application domains

- Climate science
- Surface temperature retrieval
- Satellite calibration
- Thermal remote sensing at Earth-system scale

## Why NASA JPL is a reference pole

At JPL, emissivity is not one quantity measured on one sample — it is a
global, gridded, time-resolved field produced by reconciling data from
multiple satellites. This makes JPL the reference institution for any
discussion of emissivity at planetary scale: whenever the question is
"what is the emissivity of a region of the Earth (or Mars) in this
wavelength band, right now?", the answer traces back through JEDI and
LST&E infrastructure.
